name: MonarchAiAgentCard
title: AiAgentCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with MonarchAiAgentAvatar, Text, MonarchBadge tags in a MonarchFlowLayout and MonarchIcon list rows
summary: What an AI agent is and what it may do: its name and role, a description, capabilities, the tools it can call, the data it can see and who owns it, with optional actions; a compact variant summarises it for lists.
whenToUse: In an agent directory, an "About this agent" screen or the confirmation before enabling an agent; the compact variant for a row of agents in a list.
whenNotToUse: For just the agent's picture next to a message use MonarchAiAgentAvatar. To edit what an agent may access use MonarchAiPermissionScope. To list several agents working together use MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster.
api: init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, description: String? = nil, capabilities: [String] = [], tools: [MonarchAiAgentTool] = [], dataAccess: [String] = [], owner: String? = nil, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, variant: MonarchAiAgentCardVariant = .full, labels: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels(), @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, description: String? = nil, capabilities: [String] = [], tools: [MonarchAiAgentTool] = [], dataAccess: [String] = [], owner: String? = nil, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, variant: MonarchAiAgentCardVariant = .full, labels: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels()) where Actions == EmptyView
struct MonarchAiAgentTool { init(_ name: String, description: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchAiAgentCardLabels { init(kind:, capabilities:, tools:, dataAccess:, owner:, toolCount:) }

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent: name, role, codename and avatar URL.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on what the agent is for.

options.name: capabilities
options.description: Short capability phrases, shown as badges, such as "Drafts replies".

options.name: tools
options.description: The tools the agent can call, each with what it does. The compact card shows only their count.

options.name: dataAccess
options.description: What data the agent can read, such as "Documents in this space". Full card only.

options.name: owner
options.description: Who owns or maintains the agent. Full card only.

options.name: state
options.description: What the agent is doing now, shown on its avatar.

options.name: variant
options.description: Every section, or the compact summary for lists and pickers.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons or links at the end of the full card, such as "Start a chat".

states.name: full
states.description: Large avatar, name and role line, description, then the sections that have content: What it can do, Tools, Data it can see, Owner, and the actions.

states.name: compact
states.description: Medium avatar, name, role line and a tool count, the description and the capability badges; no other section and no actions.

states.name: idle, working, waiting, error
states.description: The agent avatar's ring and, for a state other than idle, its spoken state.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the raised surface. The name uses the subheading style in the default text colour; the role line, section headings, icons and the tool descriptions use the muted text colour; capabilities are subtle neutral badges. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's headingLevel, as, nameId and descriptionId exist for HTML structure and for the web AiAgentPicker; on iOS the name has the header trait and a picker builds its own rows. The web's owner can be any node, such as an avatar with a name; here it is text. The description is text rather than any node. The web's capability tags are MonarchBadge views. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The name and the role line are one element with the header trait; the role line always says "AI agent".
Section headings have the header trait.
Each tool is one element read as its name and what it does, built by a tested pure function.
The avatar is decorative; it reads only a state other than idle ("Working").
In the compact card the capability badges are a container named "What it can do".
edgeCases: A blank role leaves only "AI agent" on the role line.
Sections with no content are left out; a card with only an agent shows the header alone.
Long names, roles and descriptions wrap; badges flow onto new lines.
The compact card ignores dataAccess, owner and actions.

examples.title: Full card
Compact, for a list
examples.code:
MonarchAiAgentCard(
    MonarchAiAgentRef(name: "Scheduler", role: "Plans meetings"),
    capabilities: ["Finds free time"],
    tools: [MonarchAiAgentTool("Calendar"), MonarchAiAgentTool("Email")],
    state: .working,
    variant: .compact
)
